newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA LEV UP ON DOLLAR SALES FOR WAGES, TAXES.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA LEV UP ON DOLLAR SALES FOR WAGES, TAXES.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev edged up to
1,567-1,573 per dollar around 0740 GMT from the opening quotes
1,575-1,582 as lev demand was higher ahead of end-month tax and
wage payments, dealers said.
A cut in the central bank main interest rate was not seen
pressuring the lev from Friday's close at about 1,575-1,578.
"Banks and clients are selling foreign currency for levs
they need for payments of wages and taxes by the end of the
month," one dealer said.
The mark traded at 931/937 levs.
Higher foreign currency supply was expected to neutralise
possible pressure on the lev due to the main rate cut as demand
was very low and the lev was seen trading rangebound between
1,565-1,580 per dollar.
The Bulgarian National Bank cut its main interest rate to
an annual 43.08 percent from 51.48 percent, in force from
Monday.
The new lower main rate curbs yields on local floating
interest government securities, making them less attractive for
both local and foreign investors.
Dealers also said some foreign investors which have locked
up levs in local treasury securities, were likely to keep the
paper to maturity but interest in new issues due to be
auctioned today was expected to fall.
Those investors were a major source of foreign currency
supply to the local market since March.
Interest on local floating interest T-bills is pegged to
the main rate which stood at 18 percent monthly in March and
falls with each rate cut during the period to maturity.
